detail_title: Channelized Right Turns With Raised Crosswalks
title: Pedestrian Island Channelized Right Turn (Channelized Right Turns With Raised Crosswalks, Sheet 1 of 2)
summary: LADOT standard drawing S-494.1 sheet 1 of 2 as reproduced in the guide appendix. It shows a channelized right turn with a pedestrian island and a raised crosswalk without a bike lane, with the yield line, approach and departure ramps, signing and the raised crosswalk ahead sign assembly. The notes are on sheet 2. No guide detail number is printed on the sheet.
description:
Plan view, Pedestrian Island Channelized Right Turn: A right-turn slip lane curves from the through street at lower left (right-turn arrow painted in the lane, dashed lane lines on the through street) around a triangular pedestrian island and out to the cross street at upper right. A sidewalk runs along the outside of the curve. The raised crosswalk crosses the slip lane. It is drawn as heavy 2 ft white or yellow bars at 5 ft center to center (C-C), with raised crosswalk marking (Chevron III) at both ends, see S-483.1. An approach ramp lies on the entry side of the crosswalk and a departure ramp on the exit side, both referenced to note 4 (the note is on sheet 2). A yield line of triangular teeth is drawn on the slip lane ahead of the approach ramp. Dimensions shown: 20' MIN. along the outer end of the raised crosswalk next to the 12 in stop line at the cross street end, 10' MIN. across the island at the crosswalk, 10' MIN. at the approach ramp and 10' MIN. at the departure ramp. A white edge line outlines the island and the through lane. Marked pedestrian crosswalks, typical, see detail S-481.1, are drawn across the cross street (horizontal bars at top) and across the through street at left (vertical bars). A 12 in stop line with an R1-1 sign (see S-494.0) controls traffic on the cross street at the end of the slip lane. Sign posts (shown as dots) hold R1-5R with W17-1bP on the island side, R1-5L with W17-1bP on the outside curb at the approach, and the raised crosswalk ahead assembly further upstream along the outside curb.

Raised crosswalk ahead assembly detail: A W11-2 pedestrian crossing diamond sign with a rectangular plaque below reading RAISED CROSSWALK AHEAD.

Sign details: R1-5L is a yield sign symbol over the words HERE TO with a left-pointing arrow and a pedestrian figure. R1-5R is the mirror image with a right-pointing arrow. W17-1bP is a rectangular plaque reading RAISED CROSSWALK.

Title block: City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Channelized Right Turns With Raised Crosswalks, sheet 1 of 2, LADOT drawing S-494.1, approved 02-20-2020 by Seleta Reynolds, General Manager. No Supplemental Street Design Guide detail number is printed on this sheet.
notes:
No numbered notes are printed on this sheet. Note 4 is referenced and appears on sheet 2 of 2.
Callouts and labels:
- Marked pedestrian crosswalk, typical (TYP.). See detail S-481.1.
- 12 in stop line.
- R1-1, see S-494.0.
- Departure ramp, see note 4.
- Raised crosswalk, see S-483.1.
- 2 ft white or yellow, 5 ft center to center (C-C).
- Approach ramp, see note 4.
- Raised crosswalk marking (Chevron III), see S-483.1.
- R1-5R, W17-1bP.
- R1-5L, W17-1bP.
- White edge line.
- Yield line.
- Raised crosswalk ahead assembly.
- Sidewalk.
Dimensions: 20' minimum (MIN.), 10' MIN., 10' MIN.
Sign details: W11-2 with RAISED CROSSWALK AHEAD plaque, R1-5L, R1-5R, W17-1bP (RAISED CROSSWALK).

detail_title: Channelized Right Turns With Raised Crosswalks
title: Pedestrian Island Channelized Right Turn With Bike Lane (Channelized Right Turns With Raised Crosswalks, Sheet 2 of 2)
summary: LADOT standard drawing S-494.1 sheet 2 of 2 as reproduced in the guide appendix. It shows a raised crosswalk at a pedestrian island on a channelized right turn where a bike lane crosses with a 2 ft green colored bicycle crossing, the modified R1-5L MOD and R1-5R MOD yield signs, and four notes. Approach and departure ramps are at least 6 ft long, or 9 ft where WB-50 trucks or buses are expected. Green pavement is optional and recommended.
description:
Plan view, Pedestrian Island Channelized Right Turn (with bike lane): A right-turn slip lane curves from the through street at lower left (right-turn arrow, dashed lane lines and a left-turn arrow on the through street) around a pedestrian island to the cross street at upper right. A grass buffer, a one-way bike lane (gray, with arrow and bicycle symbols, to be green colored) and a sidewalk run along the outside of the curve in that order from the roadway outward. The bike lane turns and crosses the slip lane beside the pedestrian crossing. Marked bike lane and white edge lines (typical) are shown on the through street at top, with a bike symbol (see notes) at the corner and a pedestrian crossing across the through street. At the island the bike lane swings toward the island and passes through a green colored surface, recommended, see note 2.

At the slip lane crossing, a raised crosswalk is drawn with raised crosswalk marking (Chevron III), see S-483.1, at each end, 2 ft white or yellow bars at 5 ft center to center (C-C) for the pedestrian crossing and 2 ft green colored bicycle crossing bars at 5 ft C-C beside it. Approach ramp and departure ramp are referenced to note 4. Dimensions shown: 20' MIN. along the raised crosswalk at the island end, 10' MIN. at the approach ramp, and 10' MIN. at the departure ramp. A 12 in stop line and an R1-1 sign are at the cross street end. Yield line teeth are drawn on the slip lane at the approach ramp. Marked pedestrian crosswalk, typical, see S-481.1. Signs on posts: R1-5R MOD with W17-1bP at the approach on the island side, R1-5L MOD with W17-1bP at the approach on the bike lane side, and the raised crosswalk ahead assembly further upstream along the bike lane.

Sign details: R1-5L MOD is a yield sign symbol over HERE, with a left-pointing arrow and the words TO followed by a bicycle symbol and a pedestrian figure. R1-5R MOD is the mirror image with a right-pointing arrow. W17-1bP is a rectangular plaque reading RAISED CROSSWALK.

Notes: four notes appear at the lower right of the sheet and are transcribed below.

Title block: City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Channelized Right Turns With Raised Crosswalks, drawing no. S-494.1, sheet 2 of 2. Notes 3 refers to Supplemental Street Design Guide Detail 100 and Detail 600, but no single detail number is printed as this sheet's own number.
notes:
1. Bike lane symbols are recommended to clarify the intended operation of the bike lane space.
2. Optional use of green colored pavement to enhance visibility and conspicuity of bicycle lane. Green colored pavement may be installed for the entire length of the bicycle lane or for only a portion (or portions) of the bicycle lane. All green colored pavement should comply with FHWA Interim Approval for Optional Use of Green Colored Pavement for Bike Lanes (IA-14) and approved by LADOT.
3. See City of Los Angeles Supplemental Street Design Guide, Detail 100 and Detail 600 for pedestrian/bicyclist island and raised crosswalk details.
4. Approach and departure ramps should be a minimum of 6' in length. Where WB-50's or buses are expected the ramp length should be 9' minimum.
Callouts and labels: marked bike lane, bike symbol (see notes), white edge lines (TYP.), pedestrian crossing, green colored surface recommended (see note 2), R1-5R MOD with W17-1bP, R1-5L MOD with W17-1bP, 20' MIN., 10' MIN. (two), marked pedestrian crosswalk TYP. see S-481.1, 12 in stop line, R1-1, grass buffer, sidewalk, bike lane, 2' green colored bicycle crossing 5' center to center (C-C), 2' white or yellow 5' C-C, raised crosswalk marking (Chevron III) see S-483.1, approach ramp (see note 4), departure ramp (see note 4), bike lane symbol TYP., raised crosswalk ahead assembly.

title: Type II Floating Bus Bulb, Bike Lane Integrated with Street Crossing (Bus Bulbs, Sheet 1 of 4)
summary: LADOT standard drawing S-523.0 sheet 1 of 4 for Type II floating bus bulbs where a Class IV bike lane passes behind the bulb and is integrated with the street crossing. It gives a street elevation plan, an intermediate elevation plan with bicycle ramps, and a section with shelter and railing placement guidance. The bulb is 8 ft minimum wide, the bike lane 5 ft minimum, and bicycle ramps are 12.5 percent maximum slope. The notes referenced are on sheet 4.
description:
Plan view, Type II Floating Bus Bulb Street Elevation, Bike Lane Integrated with Street Crossing: The bus bulb is a raised island along the street edge (street shown above), with the Class IV bike lane (gray, green colored surface recommended, see note 2, with arrow and bicycle lane symbol) passing behind it between the bulb and an existing sidewalk (5' min. width, see note 7). A 10 ft dimension is shown from the crosswalk to the start of the bulb, and an 8' MIN. width is shown across the bulb (see notes 5, 10 and 11). The bus bulb length is shown across the top, see note 6. At the left end a 24 in white or yellow crosswalk of three bars lies across the street, and a 12 in white or yellow crosswalk with a bicycle yield line (typical, shown as arrow teeth) crosses the bike lane at each end of the bulb. A rounded nose at each end carries R9-6 and OM1-1 signs. A red curb runs along the street side. Dashed boxes mark the 12' x 4' or 5' x 8' min. clear zone for the rear boarding and alighting area (see note 8), the potential bus shelter location (see note 3), and the 5' x 8' min. forward boarding and alighting area (see note 5) at the forward end. Detectable surfaces (stippled) are drawn at the crossing landing. A cross street crosswalk of three vertical bars is at left.

Plan view, Type II Floating Bus Bulb Intermediate Elevation Bike Lane: Same layout as the street elevation plan, but with a bicycle ramp at each end of the bike lane, labeled bicycle ramp 12.5% max. slope, and bicycle ramp marking (Chevron IV) (typical). The bike lane crossing at each end uses a 12 in white or yellow crosswalk with bicycle yield line (typical). The same labels apply: 24 in white or yellow crosswalk, 10' from crosswalk, 8' MIN. (see notes 5, 10 and 11), bus bulb length see note 6, R9-6 and OM1-1, red curb, class IV bike lane, 5' min. width existing sidewalk see note 7, potential bus shelter location (see note 3), 5' x 8' min. forward boarding and alighting area (see note 5), 12' x 4' or 5' x 8' min. clear zone for rear boarding and alighting area (see note 8), green colored surface recommended, see note 2, and bicycle lane symbol.

Section, Shelter and Railing Placement Guidance: A cross section from the street side to the bike lane, shows the bus bulb at left with its curb, a bus shelter with a curved roof, a pedestrian handrail (see notes 1 and 12 and S-463), then the bike lane and sidewalk at right stepping down beyond a second curb. Dimensions: 24" MIN from the bulb curb face to the shelter canopy, 18" from the bike lane face of curb to the shelter rear support post, 10" MIN from the bike lane face of curb to the pedestrian handrail, and an accessible route of 4' MIN, 5' PREF between the bulb curb and the shelter (see notes 10 and 12 on sheet 4).

Sign details: R9-6 is a bicycle symbol over the words YIELD TO PEDS. OM1-1 is a diamond object marker with nine circles.

title: Constrained Type II Bus Bulb, Raised Bike Lane, and Raised Bike Lane with Narrow Boarding and Alighting Area (Bus Bulbs, Sheet 2 of 4)
summary: LADOT standard drawing S-523.0 sheet 2 of 4 showing two constrained Type II bus bulb layouts where the bike lane is raised to the bulb level and passes through the boarding area. One has a full boarding area and the other a narrow one with 4 ft and 3 ft minimum widths and plastic bollards on the street side. Both use 12.5 percent maximum bicycle ramps, 2 ft detectable warning surfaces and crosswalks aligned with the bus doors. Notes are on sheet 4.
description:
Plan view, Constrained Type II Bus Bulb, Raised Bike Lane: A bike lane runs left to right (arrow and bicycle lane symbol) at the street edge and rises up a bicycle ramp (12.5% max. slope) with a bicycle ramp marking (Chevron IV) (typical) onto the bus bulb, where the bike lane surface is raised, gray and recommended to be green colored (see note 2). The bike lane continues through the full length of the bulb and drops down a second bicycle ramp at the right end, 12.5% max. slope, back to the street bike lane. Across the raised bike lane two 12 in white or yellow crosswalks aligned with bus doors (typical) are drawn, each with a bicycle yield line (typical, arrow teeth), one at the rear door and one at the forward door. Dashed boxes mark the 12' x 4' or 5' x 8' min. clear zone for the rear boarding and alighting area (see note 8) and the 5' x 8' min. forward boarding and alighting area (see note 5). Bus bulb length, see note 6, is dimensioned across the top. A red curb (see note 11) lies along the street side. A 2 ft wide detectable warning surface (typical) runs along the sidewalk edge of the raised bike lane and at the ramp ends. A bus stop sign stands at the right end and a 5' x 3' directional indicator strip (optional) lies on the sidewalk side at the forward area. The potential bus shelter location (see note 4) is on the sidewalk. An R9-6 and OM1-1 sign stands at the bulb entrance, with a sidewalk strip and a street label (STREET, SIDEWALK, BIKE LANE).

Plan view, Constrained Type II Bus Bulb, Raised Bike Lane with Narrow Boarding and Alighting Area: Same elements, with the street side of the bike lane protected by plastic bollards or plastic posts (typical) set in a hatched buffer before the ramp, a Class IV bike lane, and a narrow boarding strip between the street curb and the raised bike lane. Vertical dimensions across the narrow strip are 4' (MIN) and 3' (MIN). Other labels: bicycle ramp 12.5% max. slope, bicycle ramp marking (Chevron IV) (typical), bicycle lane symbol, green colored surface recommended, see note 2, R9-6 and OM1-1, red curb (see note 11), 12 in white or yellow crosswalk aligned with bus doors (typical), 2 ft wide detectable warning surfaces (typical), 5' x 3' directional indicator strip (optional), bus stop sign, potential bus shelter location (see note 4), 5' x 8' min. forward boarding and alighting area (see note 5), 12' x 4' or 5' x 8' min. clear zone for rear boarding and alighting area (see note 8), bus bulb length see note 6.

Sign details: R9-6 is a bicycle symbol over YIELD TO PEDS. OM1-1 is a diamond object marker with nine circles.

Title block: City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Bus Bulbs, sheet 2 of 4, drawing no. S-523.0.
notes:
No numbered notes are printed on this sheet. Notes 2, 4, 5, 6, 8 and 11 are referenced and appear on sheet 4 of 4.
Callouts and labels: bicycle ramp 12.5% maximum (MAX.) slope. Bicycle ramp marking (Chevron IV) (TYP). title: Bus Bulbs Notes (Bus Bulbs, Sheet 4 of 4)
summary: LADOT standard drawing S-523.0 sheet 4 of 4, a notes-only sheet for the bus bulb drawings. It sets requirements for boarding and alighting areas (5 ft by 8 ft forward, 12 ft by 4 ft rear, 2 percent maximum slope), 4 ft clear accessible routes around shelters, minimum bulb length from the table on sheet 3, red curb along the full bulb, and handrail and setback dimensions. Note 1 points to Detail 400.
description: Notes sheet: This sheet has no drawing. It carries the general notes 1 through 12 that apply to the bus bulb plans on sheets 1 and 2 and the length table on sheet 3 of drawing S-523.0. The notes cover the guide reference (Detail 400), optional green colored pavement, bus shelter placement on bulbs and on sidewalks, the forward and rear boarding and alighting areas, bus bulb length rules, sidewalk width, shelter and handrail setbacks, and red curb requirements. The title block reads City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Bus Bulbs, drawing no. S-523.0, sheet 4 of 4.
notes:
1. See City of Los Angeles Supplemental Street Design Guide, Detail 400 for bus bulb details.
2. Optional use of green colored pavement to enhance visibility and conspicuity of bicycle lane. Green colored pavement may be installed for the entire length of the bicycle lane or for only a portion (or portions) of the bicycle lane. All green colored pavement should comply with FHWA Interim Approval for Optional Use of Green Colored Pavement for Bike Lanes (IA-14), and approved by LADOT.
3. Bus shelters located on bus bulbs must be chosen and located to maintain a minimum 4 foot clear accessible path between the shelter, crosswalks, and bus boarding and alighting areas.
4. Bus shelters located on sidewalks must be chosen and located to maintain a minimum 4 foot clear accessible path between the shelter, crosswalks, and bus boarding and alighting areas. Bus shelters shall not be placed on constrained bus bulbs. They must be placed on the sidewalks, if used.
5. A minimum 5-foot wide by 8-foot deep boarding and alighting area, with a maximum slope of 2% in any direction, is required at forward loading area adjacent to the bus door. The 8-foot depth may include the adjacent curbline, but is exclusive of any railing or battered curb space. As such the physical width of the constructed bus bulb may need to exceed 8 feet. A 4-foot minimum clear accessible route must be provided between the boarding and alighting area and the sidewalk. An accessible route must also be provided between any provided bus shelters and the boarding and alighting area. If a bus bulb serves multiple transit vehicle stops simultaneously, boarding and alighting areas must be provided at each vehicle door and accessible routes provided accordingly.
6. The minimum bus bulb length is identified in the table on sheet 3, but the preferable length is based on the length of the bus(es) expected to use the bus stop. If multiple buses are expected to use the stop at the same time, the length should be based on the bus length(s) with 20 feet of separation between the buses. The length of a bus bulb is exclusive of all pedestrian ramps.
7. At locations where the sidewalk is less than 5 feet in width, a constrained bus bulb should be considered.
8. A minimum 12-foot x 4-foot clear space, with a maximum slope of 2% in any direction is recommended at all rear bus doors. If the rear door serves as the wheelchair accessible loading door, a 5-foot x 8-foot loading area is required.
9. See table on sheet 3 of 4 for DASH and Metro bus details and the corresponding minimum and recommended bus bulb lengths.
10. A minimum of 24 inch setback is needed from the face of curb to a bus shelter canopy if provided. A minimum of 18 inch setback is recommended from a bike lane face of curb to the face of any rear support posts. The selection of bus shelter types and bus bulb widths must be coordinated to ensure clearances and necessary accessible routes are provided.
11. Bus bulbs shall have red curb along their entire length adjacent to the street. Additional red curb prior to and after the bus bulb may be required by LADOT.
12. A handrail is required if drop-off from the bus bulb to the adjacent bike lane exceeds 8 inches. A minimum of 10 inch setback is needed from a bike lane face of curb to the face of pedestrian hand rail on the bus bulb.

title: Mini-Roundabouts (Yield Control) (Mini-Roundabouts and Neighborhood Traffic Circles, Sheet 1 of 4)
summary: LADOT standard drawing S-524.0 sheet 1 of 4 showing a four-leg mini-roundabout with yield control. It shows a center island, splitter islands, dashed entrance lines, arrows, crosswalks set back 20 ft, and the sign layout with W11-2, R1-2, R6-5P, W2-6 and plaques placed 100 ft and 200 ft back. Mountable splitter islands are preferred, and notes 1 to 7 are on the sheet, with note 7 citing Detail 710.
description:
Plan view, Mini-Roundabouts: A four-leg intersection of two streets (the street name 7TH AVE. is shown on a plaque) with a circular center island at the middle, a dashed circle marking the circulating roadway, and a splitter island on each approach. The center island is gray, labeled center island mountable or painted, see note 1 and see sheet 2, with a 4 in solid yellow edge line 1 ft off the mountable center island. Circulating arrows (solid white arrow symbols, optional for raised islands, required for painted islands) are drawn around the center island. Each approach shows a mountable splitter island (gray, tapering) with a solid white edge line and a 4 in solid yellow edge line 1 ft off the mountable splitter island. One approach (east) shows the optional splitter island formed by two sets of double yellow lines, see note 1 on sheet 2. A dashed white entrance line, 12 in wide, 2 ft long at 2 ft gap, is drawn across each entry. Crosswalk markings (see note 6) cross each approach, set back 20' (TYP) from the circulating roadway. Curb returns at each corner are shown with a non-walkable area (cobble hatch) between the curb and the sidewalk and new curb ramps at each crosswalk. On the south approach a YIELD word marking with yield line teeth is shown (optional), and a red curb, see DOT Std Plan S-481, is shown along the approach curb. Dimensions on the south approach: 100' and 200' measured back from the crosswalk, and 32' shown between the XING and PED pavement legends (PED XING), which are drawn on the lane.

title: Crossing Islands Notes (Crossing Islands, Sheet 5 of 5)
summary: LADOT standard drawing S-525.0 sheet 5 of 5, a notes-only sheet for the crossing island drawings. It covers bollard placement (6 in behind the edge line, 24 in to 60 in spacing, at least three), push buttons, detectable warning depth (36 in for islands 8 ft or wider, 24 in for 6 ft to 8 ft), refuge width (6 ft minimum, 8 to 10 ft preferred), RPM spacing and a 30 ft limit on total crossing length. Note 11 cites Detail 500.
description: Notes sheet: This sheet has no drawing. It carries general notes 1 through 11 for the crossing island plans on sheets 1 to 4 of drawing S-525.0. The notes cover bollards, colored pavement, pedestrian push buttons, detectable warning surfaces, median opening and approach noses, refuge width, diagonal ramps, landscaping, raised pavement markers and the maximum total crossing length. The title block reads City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Crossing Islands, sheet 5 of 5, drawing no. S-525.0.
notes:
1. Bollards shall be located 6 inches behind the edge line. Bollards may be spaced between 24 inches and 60 inches to ensure a minimum of three bollards are provided. An even spacing between bollards should be selected. Bollards should not be located within a crosswalk or parking lane.
2. The pavement surface may be colored to enhance the contrast between the adjacent travelled way and the curb extension with materials approved by City.
3. At signalized intersections, if the crossing island is at least 6 feet wide, then a pedestrian push button may be provided within the crossing island with LADOT approval. Push buttons should be located at the center of the island, but wider islands may necessitate two push buttons closer to the edge of the island. Push buttons should be located within 18 inches from curb face. If crossing islands are less than 6 feet wide, then pedestrian crossing signals must be timed to allow complete crossing and no push buttons shall be located in the crossing island.
4. Detectable warning surfaces shall be used if crossing island serves as a pedestrian refuge. Detectable warning shall be 36" deep when the crossing island is 8' or more in width. Between 6' and 8', the detectable warning shall be 24" deep. The detectable warning shall be placed at the edges of the pedestrian island or cut-through median, and shall be separated by 24" minimum of walking surface without detectable warnings.
5. If the pedestrian median opening is greater than 20 feet wide, then a bollard may be considered to prevent vehicles from encroaching into the pedestrian refuge space. Narrowing the pedestrian median opening to less than the crosswalk width may be considered in order to create sufficient space for an approach nose.
6. A minimum of 6 foot width is required to provide pedestrian refuge. Widths of 8 to 10 feet are preferred where pedestrian volumes are high, where people with mobility devices cross, or where bicyclists cross. The minimum width is 4 feet, below which a hardened centerline is preferred where it is desired to slow left-turning motorists.
7. When diagonal ramps are present, an approach nose may be added by narrowing the crossing width (see note 5). When this is not desirable, a rubberized mountable approach nose shall be used instead.
8. Landscaping of crossing islands shall follow Section E 467.3 of the Bureau of Engineering Street Design Manual.
9. Raised pavement markers (RPMs) one-way clear (white) or one-way amber (yellow) spaced 2' center-to-center may be installed on the crossing island depending on its location.
10. The total length of the crossing islands and crosswalk shall be limited to 30 feet or less on streets with only one through lane in each direction.
11. See City of Los Angeles Supplemental Street Design Guide, Detail 500 for crossing island details.

summary: LADOT standard drawing S-527.0 sheet 2 of 3 showing a Type II protected intersection corner with a corner refuge island, a 9 ft minimum separated bikeway and 5 ft minimum bike lane, and a temporary or retrofit curb extension with a diagonal ramp built from painted lines and bollards. Radii are 25 ft, crosswalk setbacks 6 ft maximum and 24 in minimum, and the retrofit hatch lines are 12 in at 45 degrees and 5 ft on center. Notes are on sheet 3.
description:
Plan view, Type II Protected Intersection with Directional Ramps: A corner of an intersection with a bikeway wrapping around the corner. A quarter-circle corner island (concrete) sits at the corner behind an 8" wide white edge line, with a gray hatched area of 12" wide white lines (see note 7) between the island and the curb return. A second narrow pedestrian refuge island sits beside the crosswalk on the near street, with a 12" stop bar and W11-15 (optional) sign. The bike lane (gray, green colored surface recommended, see note 6) carries a bicycle lane symbol and arrow with yield teeth at the crosswalk and passes between the islands. Detectable warning surfaces, see S-442 for detail, are shown at the crosswalk and refuge. 12" white crosswalk and curb are labeled, and 12" white stop line, see note 5, is at the corner island. A second W11-15 (optional) is at the far right island. Dimensions: 6' MAX. from the corner island to the crosswalk refuge, 24" MIN. at the crosswalk and refuge (two locations), 25'R and 25'R curb radii on the far right island, 9' MIN. width of the separated bikeway corner area and 5' MIN. width of the bike lane. A bicycle lane symbol and arrow sit in the bike lane at the right.

Plan view, Temporary/Retrofit Curb Extension with Diagonal Ramp: A corner extension made of painted lines: an 8" solid white edge line with radius (see note 1) at the corner, contrasting colored surface see note 3 (optional) as a small gray pad with channelizing bollards (optional, see note 2) at the corner, and a long extension beside a 12" stop bar filled with 12" solid white lines at 45 degrees spaced at 5' o.c. (on center), 8" solid white edge line, and channelizing bollards (optional). A 48" MIN dimension is shown at the diagonal ramp. A second hatched extension on the cross street is labeled match parking restriction, with contrasting colored surface, see note 3 (optional), and a MATCH PARKING RESTRICTION dimension is shown along each extension length.

Title block: City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Curb Extensions, sheet 2 of 3, drawing no. S-527.0, approved 02-20-2020 by Seleta Reynolds, General Manager. Notes 1 to 7 appear on sheet 3 of 3.
notes:
No numbered notes are printed on this sheet. Notes 1 through 7 are referenced and appear on sheet 3 of 3.
Callouts, protected intersection: W11-15 (optional), two locations. 12" white stop line, see note 5. Green colored surface recommended, see note 6. Bicycle lane symbol. 8" wide white edge line. 12" white crosswalk. 12" wide white line, see note 7. Detectable warning surfaces, see S-442 for detail. Curb. 12" stop bar. Dimensions 6' maximum (MAX.), 24" minimum (MIN.), 25'R and 25'R curb radii, 9' MIN. and 5' MIN.
Callouts, temporary/retrofit curb extension: 8" solid white edge line; radius, see note 1. Contrasting colored surface, see note 3 (optional). Channelizing bollards (optional), see note 2. 12" solid white lines, 45 degrees spaced at 5' on center (O.C.). 48" MIN. Match parking restriction (two locations). 12" stop bar.

title: Curb Extensions Notes (Curb Extensions, Sheet 3 of 3)
summary: LADOT standard drawing S-527.0 sheet 3 of 3, a notes-only sheet for the curb extension drawings. It covers corner radius policy, bollard placement (6 in behind the edge line, 24 in to 60 in spacing, at least three), colored pavement, stop line placement, optional green pavement under IA-14 and optional 12 in white lines (three preferred). Note 4 cites Detail 200.
description: Notes sheet: This sheet has no drawing. It carries general notes 1 through 7 for the curb extension plans on sheets 1 and 2 of drawing S-527.0. The notes cover corner radius, bollards, pavement coloring, the guide reference (Detail 200), stop line placement, optional green colored pavement and optional 12 in white lines. The title block reads City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Curb Extensions, sheet 3 of 3, drawing no. S-527.0.
notes:
1. The design radius should be established following the City's corner radius policy. Option to identify with a white edge line.
2. Where bollards are provided, the design radius must allow the design vehicle to turn without striking the bollards. This can be accomplished by marking the corner radius with a white edge line and locating the bollards six inches behind the edge line. Bollards may be spaced between 24 inches and 60 inches to ensure a minimum of three bollards are provided. An even spacing between bollards should be selected. Bollards should not be located within a crosswalk or parking lane.
3. The pavement surface may be colored to enhance the contrast between the adjacent traveled way and the curb extension with materials approval by the City.
4. See City of Los Angeles Supplemental Street Design Guide, Detail 200 for curb extension details.
5. Where stop line is required, it should be placed near the edge of the crossing roadway, located outside the path of turning vehicles.
6. Optional use of green colored pavement to enhance visibility and conspicuity of bicycle lane. Green colored pavement may be installed for the entire length of the bicycle lane or for only a portion (or portions) of the bicycle lane. All green colored pavement should comply with FHWA Interim Approval for Optional Use of Green Colored Pavement for Bike Lanes (IA-14) and approved by LADOT.
7. Optional 12" wide white lines, perpendicular to white edge line. If used, minimum of three (3) lines is preferred.
